text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy. ----SERBIA
POLITIKA
- Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic opens construction of 71-km stage of trans-Yugoslav highway from Subotica to Feketic (single carriageway, with stop lanes)
- Injection of fresh capital into banks and privatization are essential to rescue the banking system, says National Bank Vice-Governor Ratko Banovic
- Yugoslav economy managed to find local substitutes for 6,000 previously imported products since 1991 and subsequent international sanctions, says the Chamber of Commerce vice- -president
- Serbian thermal power plants in worsening state, major pollution-cutting work needed
- Printing fresh money to finance budget impermissible, says Yugoslav Finance Minister Bozidar Gazivoda, adding: "new 100-dinar bills have already been printed".
- Zmaj of Belgrade to deliver 200 harvesters to China by May in barter-for-oil deal
NASA BORBA
- Sources say serious split in Montenegrin leadership expected at ruling party's meeting today.

- Former Russian foreign minister Andrei Kozyrev, now a deputy in the Russian parliament, said that "Milan Panic is an exceptional figure and well known politician in Russia who proved in practice that he can lead Yugoslavia out of the profound social and economic crisis."
- Serbian opposition threats to boycott elections if media scene is not fully liberalized.
- Serious split in Bosnian Serbs' ruling party, which tried to oust Biljana Plavsic from post of Bosnian Serb Republic president
- New shooting of Serbian policeman in Kosovo.
- Government says privately-owned BK-TV operating without valid permits ; opposition says this is latest move in crackdown on independent media
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- "If the Croatian side agrees with the proposal on dual citizenship for Serbs in border zones on the Danube, we will participate in the elections on April 13," says eastern Slavonia Serb leader Vojislav Stanimirovic.
- Patriarch Pavle to visit Dalj, eastern Slavonia, on Tuesday for session of Serbian Orthodox Church Synod.

- Although some banks have reduced monthly interest on credits to 3.25 percent, the problem of lack of money for credits remains. Interest three to four times higher on the money market, but demand exceeds supply of money.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Serbian government to issue tourist passes valid 30 days instead of entry visas to promote tourism.
BORBA
- Salvation for Yugoslavia's economy lies in increased production and improved quality, politics must be separated from economy, says Yugoslav Economy Minister Rade Filipovic.
DEMOKRATIJA
- Sources say Slobodan Milosevic will be the new Yugoslav president, Momir Bulatovic the new prime minister and Zeljko Simic the Socialist candidate for Serbia's president. ----MONTENEGRO
POBJEDA

- Opposition People's Party president Novak Kilibarda broke up the party's central board and local organs, and called an extraodrinary congress for next month. Deputy president Bozidar Bojovic stripped Kilibarda of his presidential powers and moved against other leading party members.
- Montenegrin Government set aside seven million dinars for tourist propaganda in 1997, and expects a further 1.9 million worth of advertising to come from the holiday sector.
- The government also earmarked 39 million dinars for agricultural development, one-third going towards purchasing milk from small farmers.

- Education minister Dragan Kujovic says government is looking into religious education in schools -- Orthodox and Moslem leaders want religion back in schools, while Catholic church prefers Sunday school. -- Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 2224254
